answer: Reserve one seat on every five-seat panel for a tough grader: an account whose average score over its last 50 seals is in the strictest third of active graders, with alignment of 75% or better. The other four seats get drawn like now. A farm passing its own fluff about quartz countertops or a cedar trellis kit now needs 3 of the 4 open seats, since the tough seat reads it cold. Getting its accounts into that tier takes weeks of grading real answers harshly and still matching juries, like failing a vague shale lease pitch, for every single account.
